name: ocp
desc: UNIX port of the Open Cubic Player
why: The Open Cubic Player is a classic tracker-module music player with a dense, old-school interface worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: OCP is a UNIX port of the Open Cubic Player, a text-mode player for tracker music modules. It takes module files in the many tracker formats the original supported and plays them through sound hardware. The original was a DOS-era player, and this port adds terminal (ncurses), X11 and SDL front ends. The homepage describes the port as incomplete and beta-quality. The package metadata lists four executables: ocp, ocp-curses, ocp-sdl3 and ocp-vcsa.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Stian, wanted the original Cubic Team player, which was binary-only freeware from around December 1994 and later released under the GPL, to compile and run on Linux and other UNIX systems. He began the work at Christmas 2003 to keep the code useful after the project had largely died off.
brief.how_it_works: The port is being converted gradually from the original DOS-era code to POSIX, with some parts rewritten using gcc inline assembler. The homepage does not describe the audio pipeline or the front-end architecture in detail.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew needs only brew update and brew install ocp. The homepage also lists FreeBSD ports and packages, DragonFly BSD DPorts, Arch Linux via the AUR, Debian and Ubuntu packages, Fedora packages, Fink, and Gentoo. The Gentoo ebuilds are not accepted upstream, so a manual overlay is needed. The page says OpenSUSE needs a maintainer. Red Hat users are pointed to a .spec file in the source repo that the author says needs work. Other UNIX variants must build from source. Background images are optional: copy them into the ocp directory and list their filenames in the cp.ini configuration file. Downloadable Würfel-mode animations are hosted on HTTPS. Help is available on IRC at #ocp on Libera.Chat.
brief.standout: The project story is unusual: a 1994 binary-only DOS-era player was revived by a single developer who spent two months getting first characters on screen and then sound, and who documented a kernel FPU signal-handler bug found along the way. The package also includes a Würfel (cube) visual mode with its own animations.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage lists source releases from 0.1.0 up to 3.5.0, but shows no release dates. The page's own history text is dated to around 2003 and says the port is unfinished. The homepage is the only page fetched, so no last-commit date was checked.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the port is not finished, has many missing features and some strange bugs, and is usable for beta testing. Early versions had no sound, and the page does not say whether that is fixed. The Gentoo ebuild is unmerged, OpenSUSE has no maintainer, and the Fedora spec needs work. The homepage gives no licence beyond saying the original source was released under the GNU GPL. The screenshots are from older versions (v0.0.5 ncurses and v0.2.100 X11).
quotes: It was one of the best module-players if you ask me personally.
Today the project is still not ported finish, but it can be used to beta-testing.
There are still a lot of missing features and some strange bugs.
